items.text:
दुःस्वप्नं यदि पश्येत्तु वान्ते तु क्षुरकर्मणि ।
मैथुने प्रेतधूमे च स्नानं एव विधीयते ॥ १२.१ ॥
items.tr:
duḥsvapnaṃ yadi paśyettu vānte tu kṣurakarmaṇi |
maithune pretadhūme ca snānaṃ eva vidhīyate || 12.1 ||
items.en: If one has a bad dream, after vomiting, after a shave, after sex, and on touching the smoke of a funeral pyre, only a bath is prescribed.

items.text:
अज्ञानात्प्राश्य विण्मूत्रं सुरासंस्पृष्टं एव च ।
पुनः संस्कारं अर्हन्ति त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः ॥ १२.२ ॥
items.tr:
ajñānātprāśya viṇmūtraṃ surāsaṃspṛṣṭaṃ eva ca |
punaḥ saṃskāraṃ arhanti trayo varṇā dvijātayaḥ || 12.2 ||
items.en: If the three twice-born varṇas unknowingly eat faeces or urine, or something touched by liquor, they must receive the sacred initiation again.

items.text:
अजिनं मेखला दण्डो भैक्ष्यचर्या व्रतानि च ।
निवर्तन्ते द्विजातीनां पुनः संस्कारकर्मणि ॥ १२.३ ॥
items.tr:
ajinaṃ mekhalā daṇḍo bhaikṣyacaryā vratāni ca |
nivartante dvijātīnāṃ punaḥ saṃskārakarmaṇi || 12.3 ||
items.en: In this second initiation of the twice-born, the deer skin, the girdle, the staff, living by begging, and the student vows are left out.

items.text:
विण्मूत्रभोजी शुध्यर्थं प्राजापत्यं समाचरेत् ।
पञ्चगव्यं च कुर्वीत स्नात्वा पीत्वा शुचिर्भवेत् ॥ १२.४ ॥
items.tr:
viṇmūtrabhojī śudhyarthaṃ prājāpatyaṃ samācaret |
pañcagavyaṃ ca kurvīta snātvā pītvā śucirbhavet || 12.4 ||
items.en: One who has eaten faeces or urine should perform the Prājāpatya to be purified, and take pañcagavya; after bathing and drinking it he becomes pure.

items.text:
जलाग्निपतने चैव प्रव्रज्यानाशकेषु च ।
प्रत्यावसितवर्णानां कथं शुद्धिर्विधीयते ॥ १२.५ ॥
items.tr:
jalāgnipatane caiva pravrajyānāśakeṣu ca |
pratyāvasitavarṇānāṃ kathaṃ śuddhirvidhīyate || 12.5 ||
items.en: Those who tried to die by water or fire, or who took up renunciation or a fast to death, and then came back — how is purification fixed for these varṇas?

items.text:
प्राजापत्यद्वयेनैव तीर्थाभिगमनेन च ।
वृषैकादशदानेन वर्णाः शुध्यन्ति ते त्रयः ॥ १२.६ ॥
items.tr:
prājāpatyadvayenaiva tīrthābhigamanena ca |
vṛṣaikādaśadānena varṇāḥ śudhyanti te trayaḥ || 12.6 ||
items.en: Those three varṇas are purified by two Prājāpatyas, by going to holy places, and by giving ten cows and a bull.
items.note: 'vṛṣaikādaśa' may also mean eleven bulls; the reading is uncertain.

items.text:
ब्राह्मणस्य प्रवक्ष्यामि वनं गत्वा चतुष्पथे ।
सशिखं वपनं कृत्वा प्राजापत्यद्वयं चरेत् ॥ १२.७ ॥
items.tr:
brāhmaṇasya pravakṣyāmi vanaṃ gatvā catuṣpathe |
saśikhaṃ vapanaṃ kṛtvā prājāpatyadvayaṃ caret || 12.7 ||
items.en: I will now state the rule for a Brahmin: going to the forest, at a crossroads, he should shave his head including the topknot and perform two Prājāpatyas.

items.text:
गोद्वयं दक्षिणां दद्याच्छुद्धिं स्वायंभुवोऽब्रवीत् ।
मुच्यते तेन पापेन ब्राह्मणत्वं च गच्छति ॥ १२.८ ॥
items.tr:
godvayaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadyācchuddhiṃ svāyaṃbhuvo'bravīt |
mucyate tena pāpena brāhmaṇatvaṃ ca gacchati || 12.8 ||
items.en: He should give two cows as dakṣiṇā; Svāyambhuva Manu declared this purification. He is freed from that sin and regains his Brahmin status.
items.note: dakṣiṇā: the gift or fee given to Brahmins at the end of a rite.

items.text:
स्नानानि पञ्च पुण्यानि कीर्तितानि मनीषिभिः ।
आग्नेयं वारुणं ब्राह्मं वायव्यं दिव्यं एव च ॥ १२.९ ॥
items.tr:
snānāni pañca puṇyāni kīrtitāni manīṣibhiḥ |
āgneyaṃ vāruṇaṃ brāhmaṃ vāyavyaṃ divyaṃ eva ca || 12.9 ||
items.en: The wise have declared five holy baths: the bath of fire, of water, of Brahmā, of wind, and the heavenly bath.

items.text:
आग्नेयं भस्मना स्नानं अवगाह्य तु वारुणम् ।
आपो हि ष्ठेति च ब्राह्मं वायव्यं गोरजः स्मृतम् ॥ १२.१० ॥
items.tr:
āgneyaṃ bhasmanā snānaṃ avagāhya tu vāruṇam |
āpo hi ṣṭheti ca brāhmaṃ vāyavyaṃ gorajaḥ smṛtam || 12.10 ||
items.en: The fire bath is a bath with ashes; the water bath is plunging into water; the Brahmā bath is with the verse 'āpo hi ṣṭhā'; the wind bath is with dust raised by cows.

items.text:
यत्तु सातपवर्षेण तत्स्नानं दिव्यं उच्यते ।
तत्र स्नात्वा तु गङ्गायां स्नातो भवति मानवः ॥ १२.११ ॥
items.tr:
yattu sātapavarṣeṇa tatsnānaṃ divyaṃ ucyate |
tatra snātvā tu gaṅgāyāṃ snāto bhavati mānavaḥ || 12.11 ||
items.en: Bathing in rain that falls while the sun shines is called the heavenly bath. A man who bathes in it is as if he had bathed in the Ganges.

items.text:
स्नातुं यान्तं द्विजं सर्वे देवाः पितृगणैः सह ।
वायुभूतास्तु गच्छन्ति तृषार्ताः सलिलार्थिनः ॥ १२.१२ ॥
items.tr:
snātuṃ yāntaṃ dvijaṃ sarve devāḥ pitṛgaṇaiḥ saha |
vāyubhūtāstu gacchanti tṛṣārtāḥ salilārthinaḥ || 12.12 ||
items.en: When a twice-born goes to bathe, all the gods together with the ancestors follow him in the form of wind, thirsty and wanting water.

items.text:
निराशास्ते निवर्तन्ते वस्त्रनिष्पीडने कृते ।
तस्मान्न पीडयेद्वस्त्रं अकृत्वा पितृतर्पणम् ॥ १२.१३ ॥
items.tr:
nirāśāste nivartante vastraniṣpīḍane kṛte |
tasmānna pīḍayedvastraṃ akṛtvā pitṛtarpaṇam || 12.13 ||
items.en: They go back disappointed if he wrings out his cloth. So one should not wring out the cloth before offering tarpaṇa to the ancestors.
items.note: tarpaṇa: an offering of water (often with sesame) to satisfy the ancestors.

items.text:
रोमकूपेष्ववस्थाप्य यस्तिलैर्तर्पयेत्पितॄन् ।
पितरस्तर्पितास्तेन रुधिरेण मलेन च ॥ १२.१४ ॥
items.tr:
romakūpeṣvavasthāpya yastilairtarpayetpitṝn |
pitarastarpitāstena rudhireṇa malena ca || 12.14 ||
items.en: One who offers tarpaṇa to the ancestors with sesame placed on the hairs of his body — the ancestors are fed by him with blood and dirt.

items.text:
अवधूनोति यः केशान्स्नात्वा यस्तूत्सृजेन्मलम् ।
आचामेद्वा जलस्थेऽपि स बाह्यः पितृदैवतैः ॥ १२.१५ ॥
items.tr:
avadhūnoti yaḥ keśānsnātvā yastūtsṛjenmalam |
ācāmedvā jalasthe'pi sa bāhyaḥ pitṛdaivataiḥ || 12.15 ||
items.en: One who shakes his hair after bathing, who washes off dirt into the water, or who sips water while standing in the water, is shut out by the ancestors and the gods.

items.text:
शिरः प्रावृत्त्य कण्ठं वा मुक्तकच्छशिखोऽपि वा ।
विना यज्ञोपवीतेन आचान्तोऽप्यशुचिर्भवेत् ॥ १२.१६ ॥
items.tr:
śiraḥ prāvṛttya kaṇṭhaṃ vā muktakacchaśikho'pi vā |
vinā yajñopavītena ācānto'pyaśucirbhavet || 12.16 ||
items.en: With the head or throat covered, with the loincloth or topknot untied, or without the sacred thread, a person stays impure even after ācamana.
items.note: ācamana: sipping water from the palm for ritual purification.

items.text:
जले स्थलस्थो नाचामेज्जलस्थश्च बहिःस्थले ।
उभे स्पृष्ट्वा समाचान्त उभयत्र शुचिर्भवेत् ॥ १२.१७ ॥
items.tr:
jale sthalastho nācāmejjalasthaśca bahiḥsthale |
ubhe spṛṣṭvā samācānta ubhayatra śucirbhavet || 12.17 ||
items.en: One standing on land should not sip water that is in the water, and one standing in water should not sip from outside. Touching both and then sipping, one is pure in both cases.
items.note: The sense is: keep both feet where the water is taken from, or place one in each.

items.text:
स्नात्वा पीत्वा क्षुते सुप्ते भुक्त्वा रथ्योपसर्पणे ।
आचान्तः पुनराचामेद्वासो विपरिधाय च ॥ १२.१८ ॥
items.tr:
snātvā pītvā kṣute supte bhuktvā rathyopasarpaṇe |
ācāntaḥ punarācāmedvāso viparidhāya ca || 12.18 ||
items.en: After bathing, drinking, sneezing, sleeping, eating, walking in the street, and after changing clothes, one should do ācamana again even if one has already done it.

items.text:
क्षुते निष्ठीवने चैव दन्तोच्छिष्टे तथानृते ।
पतितानां च संभाषे दक्षिणं श्रवणं स्पृशेत् ॥ १२.१९ ॥
items.tr:
kṣute niṣṭhīvane caiva dantocchiṣṭe tathānṛte |
patitānāṃ ca saṃbhāṣe dakṣiṇaṃ śravaṇaṃ spṛśet || 12.19 ||
items.en: On sneezing, spitting, with food stuck in the teeth, after telling a lie, and after talking with outcastes, one should touch the right ear.

items.text:
प्रभासादीनि तीर्थानि गङ्गाद्याः सरितस्तथा ।
विप्रस्य दक्षिणे कर्णे सन्तीति मनुरब्रवीत् ॥ १२.२० ॥
items.tr:
prabhāsādīni tīrthāni gaṅgādyāḥ saritastathā |
viprasya dakṣiṇe karṇe santīti manurabravīt || 12.20 ||
items.en: Prabhāsa and the other holy places, and rivers like the Ganges, are present in the right ear of a Brahmin. Manu said this.

items.text:
अग्निरापश्च वेदाश्च सोमसूर्यानिलास्तथा ।
सर्व एव तु विप्रस्य श्रोत्रे तिष्ठन्ति दक्षिणे ॥ १२.२१(२०) ॥
items.tr:
agnirāpaśca vedāśca somasūryānilāstathā |
sarva eva tu viprasya śrotre tiṣṭhanti dakṣiṇe || 12.21(20) ||
items.en: Fire, the waters, the Vedas, the moon, the sun and the wind — all of them dwell in the right ear of a Brahmin.

items.text:
भास्करस्य करैः पूतं दिवा स्नानं प्रशस्याते ।
अप्रशस्तं निशि स्नानम् राहोरन्यत्र दर्शनात् ॥ १२.२२(२१) ॥
items.tr:
bhāskarasya karaiḥ pūtaṃ divā snānaṃ praśasyāte |
apraśastaṃ niśi snānam rāhoranyatra darśanāt || 12.22(21) ||
items.en: Bathing by day, purified by the sun's rays, is praised. Bathing at night is not praised, except when an eclipse is seen.
items.note: Eclipses were seen as Rāhu, a demon, swallowing the sun or moon.

items.text:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः कर्तव्यो राहुदर्शने ।
अन्यदा त्वशुची रात्रिस्तस्मात्तां परिवर्जयेत् ॥ १२.२३(२२) ॥
items.tr:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ kartavyo rāhudarśane |
anyadā tvaśucī rātristasmāttāṃ parivarjayet || 12.23(22) ||
items.en: Bathing, giving gifts, prayer and fire offerings should be done during an eclipse. At other times the night is impure, so one should avoid these at night.

items.text:
मरुतो वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याश्चैव देवताः ।
सर्वे सोमे प्रलीयन्ते तस्माद्दानं तु तद्ग्रहे ॥ १२.२४(२३) ॥
items.tr:
maruto vasavo rudrā ādityāścaiva devatāḥ |
sarve some pralīyante tasmāddānaṃ tu tadgrahe || 12.24(23) ||
items.en: The Maruts, Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas — all the gods merge into the moon. So gifts should be given during a lunar eclipse.

items.text:
खलयज्ञे विवाहे च संक्रान्तौ ग्रहणे तथा ।
शर्वर्यां दानं अस्त्येव नान्यत्रैव विधीयते ॥ १२.२५(२४) ॥
items.tr:
khalayajñe vivāhe ca saṃkrāntau grahaṇe tathā |
śarvaryāṃ dānaṃ astyeva nānyatraiva vidhīyate || 12.25(24) ||
items.en: At the threshing-floor sacrifice, at a wedding, at saṅkrānti, and at an eclipse, giving at night is allowed; at no other time.
items.note: saṅkrānti: the day the sun enters a new zodiac sign.

items.text:
पुत्रजन्मनि यज्ञे च तथा चात्ययकर्मणि ।
राहोश्च दर्शने दानं प्रशस्तं नान्यदा निशि ॥ १२.२६(२५) ॥
items.tr:
putrajanmani yajñe ca tathā cātyayakarmaṇi |
rāhośca darśane dānaṃ praśastaṃ nānyadā niśi || 12.26(25) ||
items.en: At the birth of a son, at a sacrifice, at death rites, and when an eclipse is seen, giving at night is approved; not at other times of night.

items.text:
महानिशा तु विज्ञेया मध्यस्थं प्रहरद्वयम् ।
प्रदोषपश्चिमौ यामौ दिनवत्स्नानं आचरेत् ॥ १२.२७(२६) ॥
items.tr:
mahāniśā tu vijñeyā madhyasthaṃ praharadvayam |
pradoṣapaścimau yāmau dinavatsnānaṃ ācaret || 12.27(26) ||
items.en: The 'great night' is the two middle praharas. In the first and the last watch of the night one may bathe as in the daytime.
items.note: prahara: one of the eight three-hour divisions of day and night.

items.text:
चैत्यवृक्षश्चितिर्यूपश्चण्डालः सोमविक्रयी ।
एतांस्तु ब्राह्मणः स्पृष्ट्वा सवासा जलं आविशेत् ॥ १२.२८(२७) ॥
items.tr:
caityavṛkṣaścitiryūpaścaṇḍālaḥ somavikrayī |
etāṃstu brāhmaṇaḥ spṛṣṭvā savāsā jalaṃ āviśet || 12.28(27) ||
items.en: A shrine tree, a funeral pyre, a sacrificial post, a Cāṇḍāla, and a seller of Soma — a Brahmin who touches these should enter water with his clothes on.

items.text:
अस्थिसंचयनात्पूर्वं रुदित्वा स्नानं आचरेत् ।
अन्तर्दशाहे विप्रस्य ह्यूर्ध्वं आचमनं भवेत् ॥ १२.२९(२८) ॥
items.tr:
asthisaṃcayanātpūrvaṃ ruditvā snānaṃ ācaret |
antardaśāhe viprasya hyūrdhvaṃ ācamanaṃ bhavet || 12.29(28) ||
items.en: Before the bones of the dead are gathered, one who weeps for them should bathe. Within the ten days a Brahmin bathes; after that, ācamana is enough.
items.note: Second half is terse; this is a best reading.

items.text:
सर्वं गङ्गासमं तोयं राहुग्रस्ते दिवाकरे ।
सोमग्रहे तथैवोक्तं स्नानदानादिकर्मसु ॥ १२.३०(२९) ॥
items.tr:
sarvaṃ gaṅgāsamaṃ toyaṃ rāhugraste divākare |
somagrahe tathaivoktaṃ snānadānādikarmasu || 12.30(29) ||
items.en: When the sun is eclipsed, all water is equal to the Ganges; the same is said of a lunar eclipse, for bathing, giving and other rites.

items.text:
कुशैः पूतं तु यत्स्नानं कुशेनोपस्पृशेद्द्विजः ।
कुशेन चोद्धृतं तोयं सोमपानसमं भवेत् ॥ १२.३१(३०) ॥
items.tr:
kuśaiḥ pūtaṃ tu yatsnānaṃ kuśenopaspṛśeddvijaḥ |
kuśena coddhṛtaṃ toyaṃ somapānasamaṃ bhavet || 12.31(30) ||
items.en: A bath purified with kuśa grass, sipping water with kuśa, and water lifted with kuśa — this is equal to drinking Soma.

items.text:
अग्निकार्यात्परिभ्रष्टाः संध्योपासनवर्जिताः ।
वेदं चाइवानधीयानाः सर्वे ते वृषलाः स्मृताः ॥ १२.३२(३१) ॥
items.tr:
agnikāryātparibhraṣṭāḥ saṃdhyopāsanavarjitāḥ |
vedaṃ cāivānadhīyānāḥ sarve te vṛṣalāḥ smṛtāḥ || 12.32(31) ||
items.en: Those who have abandoned the fire rites, who neglect the sandhyā worship, and who do not study the Veda — all of them are called vṛṣalas (Śūdras).
items.note: sandhyā: the daily prayers at dawn, noon and dusk.

items.text:
तस्माद्वृषलभीतेन ब्राह्मणेन विशेषतः ।
अध्येतव्योऽप्येकदेशो यदि सर्वं न शक्यते ॥ १२.३३(३२) ॥
items.tr:
tasmādvṛṣalabhītena brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ |
adhyetavyo'pyekadeśo yadi sarvaṃ na śakyate || 12.33(32) ||
items.en: So a Brahmin, especially, out of fear of becoming a vṛṣala, should study at least one part of the Veda if he cannot study all of it.

items.text:
शूद्रान्नरसपुष्टस्याप्यधीयानस्य नित्यशः ।
जपतो जुह्वतो वापि गतिरूर्ध्वा न विद्यते ॥ १२.३४(३३) ॥
items.tr:
śūdrānnarasapuṣṭasyāpyadhīyānasya nityaśaḥ |
japato juhvato vāpi gatirūrdhvā na vidyate || 12.34(33) ||
items.en: One whose body is nourished by the juice of a Śūdra's food has no higher path after death, even if he studies daily, prays or makes fire offerings.

items.text:
शूद्रान्नं शूद्रसंपर्कः शूद्रेण तु सहासनम् ।
शूद्राज्ज्ञानागमश्चैव ज्वलन्तं अपि पातयेत् ॥ १२.३५(३४) ॥
items.tr:
śūdrānnaṃ śūdrasaṃparkaḥ śūdreṇa tu sahāsanam |
śūdrājjñānāgamaścaiva jvalantaṃ api pātayet || 12.35(34) ||
items.en: Eating a Śūdra's food, contact with a Śūdra, sitting on the same seat with a Śūdra, and gaining knowledge from a Śūdra — these make even a shining person fall.

items.text:
यः शूद्र्या पाचयेन्नित्यं शूद्री च गृहमेधिनी ।
वर्जितः पितृदेवेभ्यो रौरवं याति स द्विजः ॥ १२.३६(३५) ॥
items.tr:
yaḥ śūdryā pācayennityaṃ śūdrī ca gṛhamedhinī |
varjitaḥ pitṛdevebhyo rauravaṃ yāti sa dvijaḥ || 12.36(35) ||
items.en: A twice-born who always has a Śūdra woman cook for him, and who has a Śūdra woman as the wife of his house, is rejected by the ancestors and gods and goes to the Raurava hell.

items.text:
मृतसूतकपुष्टाङ्गो द्विजः शूद्रान्नभोजनः ।
अहं तन्न विजानामि कां कां योनिं गमिष्यति ॥ १२.३७(३६) ॥
items.tr:
mṛtasūtakapuṣṭāṅgo dvijaḥ śūdrānnabhojanaḥ |
ahaṃ tanna vijānāmi kāṃ kāṃ yoniṃ gamiṣyati || 12.37(36) ||
items.en: A twice-born whose body is nourished by food from houses under death or birth impurity, and who eats a Śūdra's food — I do not know into what births he will go.

items.text:
गृध्रो द्वादशजन्मानि दशजन्मानि सूकरः ।
श्वयोनौ सप्तजन्मा स्यादित्येवं मनुरब्रवीत् ॥ १२.३८(३७) ॥
items.tr:
gṛdhro dvādaśajanmāni daśajanmāni sūkaraḥ |
śvayonau saptajanmā syādityevaṃ manurabravīt || 12.38(37) ||
items.en: He becomes a vulture for twelve births, a pig for ten births, and a dog for seven births. So said Manu.

items.text:
दक्षिणार्थं तु यो विप्रः शूद्रस्य जुहुयाद्धविः ।
ब्राह्मणस्तु भवेच्छूद्रः शूद्रस्तु ब्राह्मणो भवेत् ॥ १२.३९(३८) ॥
items.tr:
dakṣiṇārthaṃ tu yo vipraḥ śūdrasya juhuyāddhaviḥ |
brāhmaṇastu bhavecchūdraḥ śūdrastu brāhmaṇo bhavet || 12.39(38) ||
items.en: A Brahmin who offers oblations for a Śūdra for the sake of the fee — the Brahmin becomes a Śūdra and the Śūdra becomes a Brahmin.

items.text:
मौनव्रतं समाश्रित्य आसीनो न वदेद्द्विजः ।
भुञ्जानो हि वदेद्यस्तु तदन्नं परिवर्जयेत् ॥ १२.४०(३९) ॥
items.tr:
maunavrataṃ samāśritya āsīno na vadeddvijaḥ |
bhuñjāno hi vadedyastu tadannaṃ parivarjayet || 12.40(39) ||
items.en: A twice-born who has taken the vow of silence should not speak while seated at a meal. If someone speaks while eating, he should leave that food.

items.text:
अर्धे भुक्ते तु यो विप्रस्तस्मिन्पात्रे जलं पिबेत् ।
हतं दैवं च पित्र्यं च आत्मानं चोपघातयेत् ॥ १२.४१(४०) ॥
items.tr:
ardhe bhukte tu yo viprastasminpātre jalaṃ pibet |
hataṃ daivaṃ ca pitryaṃ ca ātmānaṃ copaghātayet || 12.41(40) ||
items.en: A Brahmin who drinks water from his plate when half the meal is eaten destroys the offering to the gods and the ancestors, and harms himself.

items.text:
भुञ्जानेषु तु विप्रेषु योऽग्रे पात्रं विमुञ्चति ।
स मूढः स च पापिष्ठो ब्रह्मघ्नः स खलूच्यते ॥ १२.४२(४१) ॥
items.tr:
bhuñjāneṣu tu vipreṣu yo'gre pātraṃ vimuñcati |
sa mūḍhaḥ sa ca pāpiṣṭho brahmaghnaḥ sa khalūcyate || 12.42(41) ||
items.en: When Brahmins are eating, the one who leaves his plate first is a fool and most sinful; he is called a Brahmin-killer.

items.text:
भाजनेषु च तिष्ठत्सु स्वस्तिकुर्वन्ति ये द्विजाः ।
न देवास्तृप्तिं आयान्ति निराशाः पितरस्तथा ॥ १२.४३(४२) ॥
items.tr:
bhājaneṣu ca tiṣṭhatsu svastikurvanti ye dvijāḥ |
na devāstṛptiṃ āyānti nirāśāḥ pitarastathā || 12.43(42) ||
items.en: Twice-born who say the blessing 'svasti' while the plates are still there — the gods are not satisfied and the ancestors are disappointed.

items.text:
अस्नात्वा नैव भुञ्जीता अजप्त्वाग्निं अहूय च ।
पर्णपृष्ठे न भुञ्जीत रात्रौ दीपं विना तथा ॥ १२.४४(४३) ॥
items.tr:
asnātvā naiva bhuñjītā ajaptvāgniṃ ahūya ca |
parṇapṛṣṭhe na bhuñjīta rātrau dīpaṃ vinā tathā || 12.44(43) ||
items.en: One should not eat without bathing, without prayer, and without making the fire offering. One should not eat on the back of a leaf, nor at night without a lamp.

items.text:
गृहस्थस्तु दयायुक्तो धर्मं एवानुचिन्तयेत् ।
पोष्यवर्गार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं न्यायवर्ती सुबुद्धिमान् ॥ १२.४५(४४) ॥
items.tr:
gṛhasthastu dayāyukto dharmaṃ evānucintayet |
poṣyavargārthasiddhyarthaṃ nyāyavartī subuddhimān || 12.45(44) ||
items.en: A householder should be kind and always think of dharma. He should be just and wise in earning what is needed for those he supports.

items.text:
न्यायोपार्जितवित्तेन कर्तव्यं ह्यात्मरक्षणम् ।
अन्यायेन तु यो जीवेत्सर्वकर्मबहिष्कृतः ॥ १२.४६(४५) ॥
items.tr:
nyāyopārjitavittena kartavyaṃ hyātmarakṣaṇam |
anyāyena tu yo jīvetsarvakarmabahiṣkṛtaḥ || 12.46(45) ||
items.en: He should support himself with wealth earned honestly. One who lives by dishonest means is excluded from all rites.

items.text:
अग्निचित्कपिला सत्री राजा भिक्षुर्महोदधिः ।
दृष्टमात्राः पुनन्त्येते तस्मात्पश्येत्तु नित्यशः ॥ १२.४७(४६) ॥
items.tr:
agnicitkapilā satrī rājā bhikṣurmahodadhiḥ |
dṛṣṭamātrāḥ punantyete tasmātpaśyettu nityaśaḥ || 12.47(46) ||
items.en: One who has built the fire altar, a tawny cow, one who performs long sacrifices, a king, a monk, and the ocean — just seeing these purifies. So one should see them always.

items.text:
अरणिं कृष्णमार्जारं चन्दनं सुमणिं घृतम् ।
तिलान्कृष्णाजिनं छागं गृहे चैतानि रक्षयेत् ॥ १२.४८(४७) ॥
items.tr:
araṇiṃ kṛṣṇamārjāraṃ candanaṃ sumaṇiṃ ghṛtam |
tilānkṛṣṇājinaṃ chāgaṃ gṛhe caitāni rakṣayet || 12.48(47) ||
items.en: Fire-drilling wood, a black cat, sandalwood, a good gem, ghee, sesame, a black antelope skin and a goat — one should keep these in the house.

items.text:
गवां शतं सैकवृषं यत्र तिष्ठत्ययन्त्रितम् ।
तत्क्षेत्रं दशगणितं गोचर्मपरिकीर्तितम् ॥ १२.४९(४८) ॥
items.tr:
gavāṃ śataṃ saikavṛṣaṃ yatra tiṣṭhatyayantritam |
tatkṣetraṃ daśagaṇitaṃ gocarmaparikīrtitam || 12.49(48) ||
items.en: Land where a hundred cows and one bull can stand freely, taken ten times over, is called a gocarma.
items.note: gocarma: a traditional measure of land given as a gift.

items.text:
ब्रह्महत्यादिभिर्मर्त्यो मनोवाक्कायकर्मजैः ।
एतद्गोचर्मदानेन मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ॥ १२.५०(४९) ॥
items.tr:
brahmahatyādibhirmartyo manovākkāyakarmajaiḥ |
etadgocarmadānena mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ || 12.50(49) ||
items.en: By the gift of this gocarma of land, a person is freed from all sins, such as killing a Brahmin, done by mind, speech or body.

items.text:
कुटुम्बिने दरिद्राय श्रोत्रियाय विशेषतः ।
यद्दानं दीयते तस्मै तद्दानं शुभकारकं ॥ १२.५१(५०) ॥
items.tr:
kuṭumbine daridrāya śrotriyāya viśeṣataḥ |
yaddānaṃ dīyate tasmai taddānaṃ śubhakārakaṃ || 12.51(50) ||
items.en: A gift given to a poor man with a family, and especially to a śrotriya, brings good results.
items.note: śrotriya: a Brahmin learned in the Veda.

items.text:
वापीकूपतडागाद्यैर्वाजपेयशतैर्मुखैः ।
गवां कोटिप्रदानेन भूमिहर्ता न शुध्यति ॥ १२.५२(५१) ॥
items.tr:
vāpīkūpataḍāgādyairvājapeyaśatairmukhaiḥ |
gavāṃ koṭipradānena bhūmihartā na śudhyati || 12.52(51) ||
items.en: One who seizes land is not purified even by building wells, step-wells and ponds, by hundreds of Vājapeya sacrifices, or by giving ten million cows.
items.note: Vājapeya: a major Vedic sacrifice.

items.text:
अष्टादशदिनादर्वाक्स्नानं एव रजस्वला ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं त्रिरात्रं स्यादुशना मुनिरब्रवीत् ॥ १२.५३(५२) ॥
items.tr:
aṣṭādaśadinādarvāksnānaṃ eva rajasvalā |
ata ūrdhvaṃ trirātraṃ syāduśanā munirabravīt || 12.53(52) ||
items.en: If a woman's period comes again before eighteen days, only a bath is needed; after that, she is impure for three nights. So said the sage Uśanas.

items.text:
युगं युगद्वयं चैव त्रियुगं च चतुर्युगम् ।
चाण्डालसूतिकोदक्या पतितानां अधः क्रमात् ॥ १२.५४(५३) ॥
items.tr:
yugaṃ yugadvayaṃ caiva triyugaṃ ca caturyugam |
cāṇḍālasūtikodakyā patitānāṃ adhaḥ kramāt || 12.54(53) ||
items.en: One yuga, two yugas, three yugas and four yugas — this is the distance to keep from a Cāṇḍāla, a woman after childbirth, a menstruating woman and an outcaste, in reverse order.
items.note: yuga here means the length of a yoke (about four cubits). 'In reverse order' is a best reading of 'adhaḥ kramāt': the outcaste one yuga, up to the Cāṇḍāla four.

items.text:
ततः संनिधिमात्रेण सचैलं स्नानं आचरेत् ।
स्नात्वावलोकयेत्सूर्यं अज्ञानात्स्पृशते यदि ॥ १२.५५(५४) ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ saṃnidhimātreṇa sacailaṃ snānaṃ ācaret |
snātvāvalokayetsūryaṃ ajñānātspṛśate yadi || 12.55(54) ||
items.en: If one comes nearer than that, one should bathe with clothes on. If one touches them unknowingly, after bathing one should look at the sun.

items.text:
विद्यमानेषु हस्तेषु ब्राह्मणो ज्ञानदुर्बलः ।
तोयं पिबति वक्त्रेण श्वयोनौ जायते ध्रुवम् ॥ १२.५६(५५) ॥
items.tr:
vidyamāneṣu hasteṣu brāhmaṇo jñānadurbalaḥ |
toyaṃ pibati vaktreṇa śvayonau jāyate dhruvam || 12.56(55) ||
items.en: A Brahmin weak in understanding who drinks water directly with his mouth even though he has hands, will surely be born as a dog.

items.text:
यस्तु क्रुद्धः पुमान्ब्रूयाज्जायायास्तु अगम्यताम् ।
पुनरिच्छति चेदेनां विप्रमध्ये तु श्रावयेत् ॥ १२.५७(५६) ॥
items.tr:
yastu kruddhaḥ pumānbrūyājjāyāyāstu agamyatām |
punaricchati cedenāṃ vipramadhye tu śrāvayet || 12.57(56) ||
items.en: If a man in anger says that his wife must not be approached, and later wants her again, he should declare this before Brahmins.

items.text:
श्रान्तः क्रुद्धस्तमोऽन्धो वा क्षुत्पिपासाभयार्दितः ।
दानं पुण्यं अकृत्वा तु प्रायश्चित्तं दिनत्रयम् ॥ १२.५८(५७) ॥
items.tr:
śrāntaḥ kruddhastamo'ndho vā kṣutpipāsābhayārditaḥ |
dānaṃ puṇyaṃ akṛtvā tu prāyaścittaṃ dinatrayam || 12.58(57) ||
items.en: If he said it while tired, angry, blinded by passion, or troubled by hunger, thirst or fear, then without giving gifts or doing good works, the penance is three days.
items.note: The link with the previous verse and the phrase 'without giving' are unclear; this is a best reading.

items.text:
उपस्पृशेत्त्रिषवणं महानद्युपसंगमे ।
चीर्णान्ते चैव गां दद्याद्ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेद्दश ॥ १२.५९(५८) ॥
items.tr:
upaspṛśettriṣavaṇaṃ mahānadyupasaṃgame |
cīrṇānte caiva gāṃ dadyādbrāhmaṇānbhojayeddaśa || 12.59(58) ||
items.en: He should bathe three times a day where great rivers meet. At the end he should give a cow and feed ten Brahmins.

items.text:
दुराचारस्य विप्रस्य निषिद्धाचरणस्य च ।
अन्नं भुक्त्वा द्विजः कुर्याद्दिनं एकं अभोजनं ॥ १२.६०(५९) ॥
items.tr:
durācārasya viprasya niṣiddhācaraṇasya ca |
annaṃ bhuktvā dvijaḥ kuryāddinaṃ ekaṃ abhojanaṃ || 12.60(59) ||
items.en: If a twice-born eats the food of a Brahmin of bad conduct who does forbidden things, he should fast for one day.

items.text:
सदाचारस्य विप्रस्य तथा वेदान्तवेदिनः ।
भुक्त्वान्नं मुच्यते पापादहोरात्रान्तरान्नरः ॥ १२.६१(६०) ॥
items.tr:
sadācārasya viprasya tathā vedāntavedinaḥ |
bhuktvānnaṃ mucyate pāpādahorātrāntarānnaraḥ || 12.61(60) ||
items.en: If a man eats the food of a Brahmin of good conduct who knows the Vedānta, he is freed from the sins of a day and night.

items.text:
ऊर्ध्वोच्छिष्टं अधोच्छिष्टं अन्तरिक्षं ऋतौ तथा ।
कृच्छ्रत्रयं प्रकुर्वीत अशौचमरणे तथा ॥ १२.६२(६१) ॥
items.tr:
ūrdhvocchiṣṭaṃ adhocchiṣṭaṃ antarikṣaṃ ṛtau tathā |
kṛcchratrayaṃ prakurvīta aśaucamaraṇe tathā || 12.62(61) ||
items.en: For impurity above or below (from eating or from excretion), for 'antarikṣa', for a woman in her season, and for a death during impurity, one should perform three Kṛcchras.
items.note: The first half is obscure (the meaning of 'antarikṣa' here is unclear); this is a best reading.

items.text:
कृच्छ्रं देव्ययुतं चैव प्राणायामशतद्वयम् ।
पुण्यतीर्थेऽनार्द्रशिरः स्नानं द्वादशसंख्यया ॥ १२.६३(६२) ॥
items.tr:
kṛcchraṃ devyayutaṃ caiva prāṇāyāmaśatadvayam |
puṇyatīrthe'nārdraśiraḥ snānaṃ dvādaśasaṃkhyayā || 12.63(62) ||
items.en: One Kṛcchra is equal to ten thousand recitations of the Gāyatrī, two hundred prāṇāyāmas, or bathing twelve times at a holy place without drying the head.
items.note: prāṇāyāma: controlled breathing exercise.

items.text:
द्वियोजने तीर्थयात्रा कृच्छ्रं एकं प्रकल्पितम् ।
गृहस्थः कामतः कुर्याद्रेतसः स्खलनं भुवि ॥ १२.६४(६३) ॥
items.tr:
dviyojane tīrthayātrā kṛcchraṃ ekaṃ prakalpitam |
gṛhasthaḥ kāmataḥ kuryādretasaḥ skhalanaṃ bhuvi || 12.64(63) ||
items.en: A pilgrimage of two yojanas counts as one Kṛcchra. A householder who on purpose spills his semen on the ground,
items.note: yojana: a measure of distance, roughly 12-15 km.

items.text:
सहस्रं तु जपेद्देव्याः प्राणायामैस्त्रिभिः सह ।
चतुर्विद्योपपन्नस्तु विधिवद्ब्रह्मघातके ॥ १२.६५(६४) ॥
items.tr:
sahasraṃ tu japeddevyāḥ prāṇāyāmaistribhiḥ saha |
caturvidyopapannastu vidhivadbrahmaghātake || 12.65(64) ||
items.en: … should recite the Gāyatrī a thousand times with three prāṇāyāmas. For a killer of a Brahmin who was learned in the four Vedas, by rule,

items.text:
समुद्रसेतुगमनं प्रायश्चित्तं विनिर्दिशेत् ।
सेतुबन्धपथे भिक्षां चातुर्वर्ण्यात्समाचरेत् ॥ १२.६६(६५) ॥
items.tr:
samudrasetugamanaṃ prāyaścittaṃ vinirdiśet |
setubandhapathe bhikṣāṃ cāturvarṇyātsamācaret || 12.66(65) ||
items.en: … the penance to prescribe is a journey to the bridge in the ocean (Setu). On the road to Setubandha he should beg from all four varṇas,
items.note: Setubandha: the bridge to Laṅkā said to have been built for Rāma, at Rāmeśvaram.

items.text:
वर्जयित्वा विकर्मस्थांश्छत्रोपानद्विवर्जितः ।
अहं दुष्कृतकर्मा वै महापातककारकः ॥ १२.६७(६६) ॥
items.tr:
varjayitvā vikarmasthāṃśchatropānadvivarjitaḥ |
ahaṃ duṣkṛtakarmā vai mahāpātakakārakaḥ || 12.67(66) ||
items.en: … avoiding those who follow wrong work, without umbrella or shoes, saying: 'I am a doer of evil, one who has committed a great sin;

items.text:
गृहद्वारेषु तिष्ठामि भिक्षार्थी ब्रह्मघातकः ।
गोकुलेषु वसेच्चैव ग्रामेषु नगरेषु वा ॥ १२.६८(६७) ॥
items.tr:
gṛhadvāreṣu tiṣṭhāmi bhikṣārthī brahmaghātakaḥ |
gokuleṣu vaseccaiva grāmeṣu nagareṣu vā || 12.68(67) ||
items.en: I, a Brahmin-killer, stand at the doors of houses begging.' He should stay in cow pens, villages or towns,

items.text:
तपो वनेषु तीर्थेषु नदीप्रस्रवणेषु वा ।
एतेषु ख्यापयन्नेनः पुण्यं गत्वा तु सागरं ॥ १२.६९(६८) ॥
items.tr:
tapo vaneṣu tīrtheṣu nadīprasravaṇeṣu vā |
eteṣu khyāpayannenaḥ puṇyaṃ gatvā tu sāgaraṃ || 12.69(68) ||
items.en: … in hermitage forests, holy places, rivers and springs, declaring his sin in these places. Then, going to the holy ocean,

items.text:
दशयोजनविस्तीर्णं शतयोजनं आयतम् ।
रामचन्द्रसमादिष्ट नलसंचयसंचितम् ॥ १२.७०(६९) ॥
items.tr:
daśayojanavistīrṇaṃ śatayojanaṃ āyatam |
rāmacandrasamādiṣṭa nalasaṃcayasaṃcitam || 12.70(69) ||
items.en: … ten yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long, built up by Nala at the command of Rāmacandra,

items.text:
सेतुं दृष्ट्वा समुद्रस्य ब्रह्महत्यां व्यपोहति ।
सेतुं दृष्ट्वा विशुद्धात्मा त्ववगाहेत सागरम् ॥ १२.७१(७०) ॥
items.tr:
setuṃ dṛṣṭvā samudrasya brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati |
setuṃ dṛṣṭvā viśuddhātmā tvavagāheta sāgaram || 12.71(70) ||
items.en: … seeing the bridge on the ocean, he removes the sin of killing a Brahmin. After seeing the bridge, pure in himself, he should bathe in the ocean.

items.text:
यजेत वाश्वमेधेन राजा तु पृथिवीपतिः ।
पुनः प्रत्यागते वेश्म वासार्थं उपसर्पति ॥ १२.७२(७१) ॥
items.tr:
yajeta vāśvamedhena rājā tu pṛthivīpatiḥ |
punaḥ pratyāgate veśma vāsārthaṃ upasarpati || 12.72(71) ||
items.en: Or a king, a lord of the earth, should perform the Aśvamedha sacrifice. When he comes back and returns to live in his home,
items.note: Aśvamedha: the royal horse sacrifice.

items.text:
सपुत्रः सह भृत्यैश्च कुर्याद्ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
गाश्चैवैकशतं दद्याच्चतुर्विध्येषु दक्षिणाम् ॥ १२.७३(७२) ॥
items.tr:
saputraḥ saha bhṛtyaiśca kuryādbrāhmaṇabhojanam |
gāścaivaikaśataṃ dadyāccaturvidhyeṣu dakṣiṇām || 12.73(72) ||
items.en: … he, with his sons and servants, should feed Brahmins and give a hundred cows as dakṣiṇā to those learned in the four Vedas.

items.text:
ब्राह्मणानां प्रसादेन ब्रह्महा तु विमुच्यते ।
सवनस्थां स्त्रियं हत्वा ब्रह्महत्याव्रतं चरेत् ॥ १२.७४(७३) ॥
items.tr:
brāhmaṇānāṃ prasādena brahmahā tu vimucyate |
savanasthāṃ striyaṃ hatvā brahmahatyāvrataṃ caret || 12.74(73) ||
items.en: By the grace of the Brahmins the Brahmin-killer is set free. One who kills a woman taking part in a Soma rite should perform the vow for killing a Brahmin.

items.text:
मद्यपश्च द्विजः कुर्यान्नदीं गत्वा समुद्रगाम् ।
चान्द्रायणे ततश्चीर्णे कुर्याद्ब्राह्मणभोजनं ॥ १२.७५(७४) ॥
items.tr:
madyapaśca dvijaḥ kuryānnadīṃ gatvā samudragām |
cāndrāyaṇe tataścīrṇe kuryādbrāhmaṇabhojanaṃ || 12.75(74) ||
items.en: A twice-born who has drunk liquor should go to a river that flows to the sea and perform the Cāndrāyaṇa; after completing it, he should feed Brahmins,

items.text:
अनडुत्सहितां गां च दद्याद्विप्रेषु दक्षिणाम् ।
सुरापानं सकृत्कृत्वा अग्निवर्णं सुरां पिबेत् ॥ १२.७६(७५) ॥
items.tr:
anaḍutsahitāṃ gāṃ ca dadyādvipreṣu dakṣiṇām |
surāpānaṃ sakṛtkṛtvā agnivarṇaṃ surāṃ pibet || 12.76(75) ||
items.en: … and give a cow with an ox as dakṣiṇā to Brahmins. One who has drunk liquor even once (on purpose) should drink liquor heated to the colour of fire;

items.text:
स पावयेदथात्मानं इहलोके परत्र च ।
अपहृत्य सुवर्णं तु ब्राह्मणस्य ततः स्वयं ॥ १२.७७(७६) ॥
items.tr:
sa pāvayedathātmānaṃ ihaloke paratra ca |
apahṛtya suvarṇaṃ tu brāhmaṇasya tataḥ svayaṃ || 12.77(76) ||
items.en: … in this way he purifies himself in this world and the next. One who has stolen a Brahmin's gold should then himself

items.text:
गच्छेन्मुसलं आदाय राजाभ्याशं वधाय तु ।
ततः शुद्धिं अवाप्नोति राज्ञासौ मुक्त एव च ॥ १२.७८(७७) ॥
items.tr:
gacchenmusalaṃ ādāya rājābhyāśaṃ vadhāya tu |
tataḥ śuddhiṃ avāpnoti rājñāsau mukta eva ca || 12.78(77) ||
items.en: … go to the king carrying a club, to be put to death. Then he gains purity, whether he dies or is set free by the king.

items.text:
कामतस्तु कृतं यत्स्यान्नान्यथा वधं अर्हति ।
आसनाच्छयनाद्यानात्संभाषात्सह भोजनात् ॥ १२.७९(७८) ॥
items.tr:
kāmatastu kṛtaṃ yatsyānnānyathā vadhaṃ arhati |
āsanācchayanādyānātsaṃbhāṣātsaha bhojanāt || 12.79(78) ||
items.en: This applies when it was done on purpose; otherwise he does not deserve death. From sharing a seat, a bed, a vehicle, conversation or a meal,

items.text:
संक्रामन्ति हि पापानि तैलबिन्दुरिवाम्भसि ।
चान्द्रायणं यावकं तु तुलापुरुष एव च ॥ १२.८०(७९) ॥
items.tr:
saṃkrāmanti hi pāpāni tailabindurivāmbhasi |
cāndrāyaṇaṃ yāvakaṃ tu tulāpuruṣa eva ca || 12.80(79) ||
items.en: … sins spread from one person to another, like a drop of oil on water. The Cāndrāyaṇa, the yāvaka diet, the tulāpuruṣa gift,
items.note: tulāpuruṣa: a gift of gold or goods equal to one's own body weight.

items.text:
गवां चैवानुगमनं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ।
एतत्पाराशरं शास्त्रं श्लोकानां शतपञ्चकम् ।
द्विनवत्या समायुक्तं धर्मशास्त्रस्य संग्रहः ॥ १२.८१(८०) ॥
items.tr:
gavāṃ caivānugamanaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam |
etatpārāśaraṃ śāstraṃ ślokānāṃ śatapañcakam |
dvinavatyā samāyuktaṃ dharmaśāstrasya saṃgrahaḥ || 12.81(80) ||
items.en: … and walking behind cows destroy all sins. This Parāśara scripture has five hundred and ninety-two verses; it is a summary of dharmaśāstra.

items.text:
यथाध्ययनकर्माणि धर्मशास्त्रं इदं तथा ।
अध्येतव्यं प्रयत्नेन नियतं स्वर्गगामिना २८८) ॥ १२.८२(८१) ॥
items.tr:
yathādhyayanakarmāṇi dharmaśāstraṃ idaṃ tathā |
adhyetavyaṃ prayatnena niyataṃ svargagāminā 288) || 12.82(81) ||
items.en: Like the duties of Veda study, this dharmaśāstra should be studied with effort and regularly by one who wishes to reach heaven.
items.note: The '288)' at the end of the source line is a stray mark, not part of the verse.
